text:
devon: Heads up — since we rolled the qkernel-v2 quantized kernel to 30% canary this morning, /v1/generate p95->p99 token latency has jumped. Not a steady CPU issue, looks correlated with KV miss rate and a small kernel-selection fallback penalty. infra-bot just fired a burn-rate alert.

lena: Ugh. timeline? what changed exactly in qkernel-v2 compared to v1?

devon: Changed kernel dispatch logic to prefer fused-attn path. Also we added aggressive int8 matmul path that falls back to fp16 if shapes mismatch. Fallback path introduces ~6-12ms extra per-token when it runs. Logs show fallback runs more often when kv_cache_miss_rate > 12%.

josh: infra-bot alert payload: 
```
ALERT: latency_burnrate_per_route (/v1/generate)
window: 10m
burnrate: 1.6x
metric_breakdown: token_queue_ms=4, kernel_ms=9, kv_miss_ms=15
```

infra-bot: Pager triggered: oncall-pager paged (sev=2) — see runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-burnrate

oncall-pager: I'm on it, pulling traces now.

maya: Quick sanity check — did traffic mix change? more long context or more streaming requests?
devon: Mix is same. Customer routing shows slight uptick in long-context requests for 1 customer, but traces show per-token penalty even for short inputs when kv miss happens (cold cache). So likely warmup behavior + fallback kernel hits.

lena: Can we tweak alerting to be token-level instead of request-level? currently it triggers on request P99 which hides kv-miss microspikes. I want a token_latency_breakdown panel in the alert payload (per-route).

josh: Agree. Proposed quick change: change alert expr to use rate(token_latency_sum[1m]) / rate(token_count[1m]) and threshold on p99_token_latency. That should make burnrate reflect per-token inflation vs long tail requests.

devon: Also adding a KV-cache warmup gauge to dashboard helped in old rollouts. Suggest adding heatmap: kv_miss_rate by pod over 5m, and correlate with kernel_fallback_rate.

infra-bot: Suggested dashboard panels created: dashboard/ops/kernel-warmup-187654 — includes token-level heatmap and per-route kpis.

maya: Practical mitigation — revert qkernel-v2 canary to 5% while we investigate, or add a short term override to prefer fp16 path when kv miss > 10%. Which is faster?

devon: Reverting to 5% now. Also will push a patch that avoids fallback by adding a pre-check for shape compat before dispatch. That should reduce fallback rate significantly.

josh: Revert done. Canary traffic back to 5% (route tags show 95% v1, 5% v2). Burnrate alert silenced for now but will resume if it spikes.

lena: For the alert change, I'm going to add an anomaly detector on token_latency_rate (simple zscore over 30m) to catch sustained micro-spikes before paging. Lower paging threshold for token-level p99 to 1.25x baseline with an auto-suppress if kv_miss_rate is > 20% (so we avoid noise during obvious cache-thrashing).

devon: Good plan. Can we also add a small synthetic that exercises cold-kv warmup pattern so regressions are caught in CI? Short script: spawn 30 cold requests with randomized prefixes and measure median token latency. If median increases > 5% vs baseline fail the rollout.

josh: I'll add the CI job to eng-runtime/canary-checks and wire the metric into the rollout pipeline.

maya: After revert, monitor p95/p99 token latency, kv_miss_rate, kernel_fallback_rate for 60m. If any > 1.4x baseline, we reopen pager.

infra-bot: Noted. Monitoring window started (60m).

devon: TL;DR: revert to 5%, add token-level burnrate alert, dashboard heatmap for kv misses and kernel fallbacks, CI cold-warmup test, and a kernel dispatch pre-check patch. Thanks all — will follow up with PRs and dashboard links. :thumbsup:
